scene_en: You are recording a video introduction for a job application. Fill in the blank: 'My name is Tanaka.'
wrong_options: 田中とおっしゃいます|田中と言います
explanation_en: 言う becomes 申す in 謙譲語II. This form lowers your own speech to the listener and is the standard way to state your name formally. おっしゃいます is 尊敬語 for the listener, which would mean the interviewer is called Tanaka, not you. 言います is polite but not keigo.

scene_en: You are writing an email to a recruiter. Fill in the blank: 'I will come to your office on Friday.'
correct_sentence: 金曜日に御社に参ります
wrong_options: 金曜日に御社にいらっしゃいます|金曜日に御社に行きます
explanation_en: 行く becomes 参る in 謙譲語II. 参ります lowers your own movement to show respect to the recipient of the email. いらっしゃいます is 尊敬語 and would mean the recruiter is going to their own office. 行きます is polite but not keigo.

scene_en: A recruiter asks who encouraged you to apply. Your professor recommended the company. Fill in the blank: 'My professor said: Please do apply.'
scene_jp: 先生が「ぜひ応募してほしい」と___。
correct_sentence: 先生が「ぜひ応募してほしい」と申しておりました
wrong_options: 先生が「ぜひ応募してほしい」とおっしゃいました|先生が「ぜひ応募してほしい」と言っていました
explanation_en: This is an ウチ/ソト case. Even though your professor is senior to you, when you speak to a recruiter (ソト), your professor is part of your in-group (ウチ). In Japanese business etiquette, you use humble forms for your own group members when speaking to outsiders. おっしゃる (尊敬語) would elevate your professor above the recruiter, which breaks this convention. 申す (謙譲語II) is the correct humble form here.

scene_en: A client calls your office asking for your manager Tanaka. Your manager is out. Fill in the blank: 'Tanaka is currently out of the office.'
correct_sentence: 田中は只今外出しております
wrong_options: 田中部長は只今外出されております|田中は只今外出しています
explanation_en: Another ウチ/ソト case. When speaking about your manager to a client, your manager is ウチ (your in-group) relative to the client (ソト). Use humble forms for ウチ members. おります is 謙譲語II for いる. Do not use the title 部長 when referring to your manager to an outsider, and avoid 外出されております (passive honorific) as it incorrectly elevates your manager to the client. 外出しています is polite but not keigo.

scene_en: A recruiter at a career fair is about to look at your portfolio. Fill in the blank: 'Please take a look.'
correct_sentence: どうぞご覧になってください
wrong_options: どうぞ拝見してください|どうぞ見てください
explanation_en: Here the recruiter is performing the action (looking), so you use 尊敬語 to honor their action. 見る becomes ご覧になる in 尊敬語. 拝見する is 謙譲語I and would lower the recruiter's action, which is disrespectful. 見てください is polite but lacks keigo.
